records.title: An alternating antimorphic Fine-Wilf theorem
records.description: For an arbitrary antimorphic involution theta, a finite word with alternating theta-periods p and q and length at least p+q-gcd(p,q) has alternating theta-period gcd(p,q). This proves the exact unnumbered conjecture after Theorem 23 on printed page 2220 of Nowotka's contribution, joint with Bischoff, to the 2010 Oberwolfach mini-workshop on combinatorics on words. The common finite extension theta(w)w has ordinary periods 2p and 2q; classical Fine-Wilf and central reflection give the alternating conclusion. A reversal example shows that the sufficient formula cannot be reduced by one uniformly; pairwise optimality is not asserted. The research note credits Fine and Wilf, the originating report and Bischoff's thesis, and compares the related Czeizler-Kari-Seki, Kari-Seki and Simpson results. A portable verification supplement preserves the submitted proof, three independent adversarial mathematical audits, complete finite-control outputs and a dated bounded priority audit. No earlier exact theorem was found in the inspected primary sources, without a global novelty or first-discovery certificate; access and version gaps are explicit. AI tools were used extensively in solving, verification, literature research, writing, computation and adversarial review. This is an unrefereed research note and has not received independent external human peer review.
